new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (4 pp., text, the PDF's metadata gives the Author 'SIL PNG Branch', created 2004-08-24; header 'Organised Phonology Data / Kube (Mongi, Hube) Language [KGF] / Morobe Province / Trans New Guinea Phylum; Finisterre-Huon Stock; Eastern Huon Subfamily / Major villages: Gemaheng'; bibliography: Lee, Yongseop & Hyunsook Lee 1990 OPD ms., Ukarumpa). On p.3, after the diphthong list, the text reads exactly: 'Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length)' / 'Stress is on the first syllable of the word.' followed by 'Syllable Patterns'. Quote is verbatim at the stated locator. Nothing else in the OPD bears on stress (no secondary stress, no tone/length claims). Cross-checked (168 pp., 2014 PDF of the…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is fixed on the initial syllable. Supporting evidence from Lee 1993:51: compound nouns form one phonological word in which only the first root bears stress (non-initial roots are unstressed), i.e. one initial stress per phonological word.
new_statements.exceptions: None in the OPD. Lee 1993:51 adds only that non-initial roots of compounds lose their stress.
new_statements.domain_note: Stated for 'the word'; Lee 1993 treats compounds as single phonological words with a single (initial) stress. No tone or contrastive length reported in the suprasegmentals section.
new_statements.identity_note: The OPD header names the variety 'Kube (Mongi, Hube) [KGF]', major village Gemaheng, Morobe Province; Lee's fieldwork (from 1988) covers Kube proper with its two dialects Kulungtfu and Yuanggeng (= Glottolog kube1244 'Kulungtfu-Yuanggeng-Tobo', ISO kgf). Tobo [tbv], which Lee 1993:11 regards as probably a Kube dialect (95% cognate), is not the variety described.
